historical_record.description: Under the 1947 recreation bond program the Recreation and Park Commission engaged William Mooser and John W. Gloe, architects, to design a Central Activities Building in Duboce Park, at Scott Street and Duboce Avenue, estimated at $200,000.

The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract to build the Central Activities, or Recreational Arts, Building at Duboce Avenue and Scott Street to Ira Larsen Company at $395,213, the lowest of three bids.
The Recreation and Park Commission approved a $1,422.50 contract with Beckwith and Langsner to design and build play equipment in place at Duboce Park.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved a professional services agreement with Timothy Downey Associates, landscape architects, to design planting, irrigation, paths and play equipment for the part of Duboce Park east of the Recreational Arts Building.

With the support of the late Supervisor Harvey Milk's staff and community groups, the Recreation and Park Commission renamed the Recreational Arts Building at 50 Scott Street, by Duboce Park, the Harvey Milk Center.

Duboce Park was to be rededicated on April 26, 1980 after a $284,000 rebuilding, with automatic irrigation, new landscaping and reshaping, a children's play area and a tennis court, designed by Timothy Downey, landscape architect.
A Harvey Milk memorial mural at the Harvey Milk Recreation Center, 50 Scott Street by Duboce Park, was to be dedicated on June 2, 1988.

Because the only space for a pit head at the east portal of the Sunset Tunnel (Duboce Avenue route) was the southwest part of Duboce Park, the Board of Park Commissioners granted the Youdall Construction Company its use for up to eighteen months, the contractor to remove trees and shrubs under Superintendent McLaren and restore the ground afterward.

On the Duboce Park site, where tons of rock had been dumped, the mounds were cleared, some of the rock built into rockeries, and the ground plowed, sown to grass and planted with shrubs to an adopted plan.
